sentence: Someone who keeps a GitHub project or a website and wants people to find it, before they publish or rewrite it, gets the words people really type into search engines put where Google and GitHub read them, with every change checked instead of taken on trust.

unfinished.item: eco-site and everything new in 0.2.0 has only run in the test suite, never a full run on a real website

sections.heading: Why can't people find my project?

picture.claim: A search only reaches a title that uses the words people type: a README title and then a web page title each go from missing searched words to having every one of them after Eco.
shows: searched words as chips, three then four
web page title before and after
words found count, of 3 and of 4

picture.claim: Eco changes only the few places search engines read, one phrase per place, on a repository page and on a web page, and leaves the rest of the text as it was.
shows: web page window with head tags
meta description, headings and link preview
places lit one at a time
name card for the lit place

sections.heading: How do I know it worked?

picture.claim: A script checks every change before the report, and after you publish it repeats the saved searches and gives each one a verdict.
Two commands install it, and it runs only when you type its command in your project: /eco:eco-readme for a README, /eco:eco-site for a website.
shows: readme command, runs on a README
site command, runs on a website
